title: Continuous-time information I: existence/finiteness and well-posedness not proved (Def 1, Thm 2)

comments.author: human
comments.body: Definition 1 defines $I=D(P\|P^{\mathrm{ref}})$ and the remark claims (Ichain) has a well-defined continuous-time limit (a transfer-entropy rate). Neither absolute continuity $P\ll P^{\mathrm{ref}}$ nor finiteness of the relative entropy is established. For continuous observation of a diffusion, the mutual information between a path and a continuously-observed functional is frequently **infinite**; indeed Theorem 2 (`thm:Imax-cont`) itself admits $I_A\to\infty$ as the dwell time $\delta\to0$. Part (a) requires $I$ to be a finite, well-posed object — or the admissible protocol class must be restricted (finite dwell time, finitely many outcomes per step) **in the definition** so that $I\le H(A)$ is well-posed by construction. The relation $I_A\le H(A)$ relies on $H(A)$ being finite, which only holds under such a restriction; this should be part of the definition, not derived afterward.
